Hi! I am an experimental Ecophysiologist, having recently completed and defended my PhD, “Growth and metabolic scaling of fish”, at DTU Aqua in Lyngby, Denmark. Being an experimental Eco-Physiologist means that I conduct experiments to understand how animals are adapted to their environment and how they respond to changes. I then use quantitative data analysis to examine how my and others' data can help explain ecological responses.

My research has mainly focused on:

-   Whole body animal energetics (determining minimum and maximum energy use and thus energetic budget)
-   How metabolic rate scales with body size 
-   Trade-offs between growth rate and energy use
-   Impact of anthropogenic changes on metabolic rate in from arctic to tropical environments
-   Measurement of protein synthesis following meal ingestion

When I am not in the lab running respiratory experiments on fish or collecting copepods in Greenland, I like to play board games or be out in nature. In fact, I am equally content sitting in my tent in a remote mountain valley in northern Sweden as I am playing board games with my friends, though in both cases I will be enjoying a good cup of tea. When I am doing neither of these things, I enjoy cooking food, with a particular fondness for making Danish ryebread, and reading lengthy fantasy books.
:::
